title: Invalid Transactions
statement:
Each string in `transactions` describes one transaction as four comma-separated fields: `name,time,amount,city`, where `time` is in minutes and `amount` is a whole number.

A transaction is **suspicious** if at least one of these holds:

- its amount is greater than 1000;
- some other transaction with the same name but a different city happened at most 60 minutes before or after it (a gap of exactly 60 still counts).

Return every suspicious transaction string, in any order. If the same string appears several times in `transactions` and is suspicious, it appears that many times in the answer. Return an empty list when nothing is suspicious.
constraints: name and city are 1 to 10 lowercase English letters
time is written in digits and is an integer from 0 to 1000
amount is written in digits and is an integer from 0 to 2000
notes:
## Intuition

The obvious check compares every pair of transactions: same name, different city, times at most 60 apart. That is O(n²). Times are whole minutes between 0 and 1000, so instead we can index the transactions by `name` and exact `time`, recording which cities appear there. A transaction then only has to look up the 121 minutes from `time - 60` to `time + 60` and ask whether any city other than its own shows up.

## Approach

1. Parse each string into `records` with numeric `time` and `amount`.
2. Build `citiesAt`: the key `"name,time"` maps to the set of cities seen for that name at that minute.
3. For each record, start with `bad = amount > 1000`.
4. If not yet bad, scan `t` from `time - 60` to `time + 60`. A set at `"name,t"` that has two or more cities, or lacks this record's `city`, proves a clash with a different city.
5. Push the original string for every bad record and return the list.

## Example 1, step by step

`citiesAt` holds `"alice,20" → {mtv}` and `"alice,50" → {beijing}`.

- `"alice,20,800,mtv"`: amount 800 is fine. Scanning minutes -40..80 reaches `"alice,50"`, whose set `{beijing}` lacks `mtv`, so it is invalid.
- `"alice,50,100,beijing"`: scanning -10..110 reaches `"alice,20"` with `{mtv}`, which lacks `beijing`, so it is invalid too.

Both strings are returned.

## Complexity

- Time: O(121 · n): one pass to index, then at most 121 hash lookups per transaction.
- Space: O(n) for the parsed records and the index.

## Pitfalls

- The window is inclusive: a gap of exactly 60 minutes counts.
- An amount of exactly 1000 is fine; only more than 1000 is suspicious.
- A clash needs a **different** city; same name, same city, same minute is harmless. That is why a set with one city equal to ours does not count.
- Return duplicates as often as they appear, and compare `time` as a number, not as text.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `records` | parsed `{ name, time, amount, city }` objects |
| `citiesAt` | `"name,time"` → set of cities at that minute |
| `invalid` | the suspicious transaction strings found so far |
| `bad` | whether record `i` is suspicious |
| `t` | a minute inside the 60-minute window |
| `cities` | the cities this name visited at minute `t` |
